items.readable_text:
Content:
To add two numbers given in scientific notation with the same power of ten, we simply add the decimal parts.

Content:
To demonstrate, let's add the numbers [MATH: 7.7\times 10^4] and [MATH: 1.2 \times 10^4.]

Content:
Since both numbers are multiplied by [MATH: 10^4,] we add the decimal parts and then multiply the result by [MATH: 10^4.] By doing this, we get

Content:
[MATH: (7.7 × 10^{4}) + (1.2 × 10^{4})|= (7.7 + 1.2) × 10^{4}; = 8.9 × 10^{4}.]

items.readable_text:
Content:
Sometimes, we'll have to adjust the final result after adding (or subtracting) numbers in scientific notation.

Content:
Suppose we wish to add [MATH: 8.1 \times 10^5] and [MATH: 6.2 \times 10^5.]

Content:
Since the numbers have the same power of [MATH: 10,] we add the decimal parts and then multiply the result by [MATH: 10^{5}.] By doing this, we get

Content:
[MATH: (8.1 × 10^{5}) + (6.2 × 10^{5})|= (8.1 + 6.2) × 10^{5}; = 14.3 × 10^{5}.]

Content:
However, the above number is not in scientific notation because [MATH: 14.3 \gt 10.]

Content:
So, we need to write [MATH: 14.3] in scientific notation as follows:

Content:
[MATH: 14.3 = 1.43 \times 10^1]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: 14.3 × 10^{5}|= (1.43 × 10^{1}) × 10^{5}; = 1.43 × (10^{1} × 10^{5}); = 1.43 × 10^{1 + 5}; = 1.43 × 10^{6}.]

Content:
So, our final answer is [MATH: 1.43 \times 10^6.]

sections.normalized_html:
Since the numbers have the same power of [MATH: 10,] we add the decimal parts and then multiply the result by [MATH: 10^{-12}.] By doing this, we get

[MATH: (7.8 × 10^{− 12}) + (5 × 10^{− 12})|= (7.8 + 5) × 10^{− 12}; = 12.8 × 10^{− 12}.]

The above number is not in scientific notation because [MATH: 12.8 \gt 10.] So, we need to write [MATH: 12.8] in scientific notation, as follows:

[MATH: 12.8 = 1.28\times 10^1]

Therefore,

[MATH: 12.8 × 10^{− 12}|= (1.28 × 10^{1}) × 10^{− 12}; = 1.28 × (10^{1} × 10^{− 12}); = 1.28 × 10^{1 − 12}; = 1.28 × 10^{− 11}.]

So, our final answer is [MATH: 1.28 \times 10^{-11}.]

sections.normalized_html:
Since the numbers have the same power of [MATH: 10,] we subtract the decimal parts and then multiply the result by [MATH: 10^{-9}.] By doing this, we get

[MATH: (2.7 × 10^{− 9}) − (3 × 10^{− 9})|= (2.7 − 3) × 10^{− 9}; = − 0.3 × 10^{− 9}.]

The above number is not in scientific notation because [MATH: 0.3 \lt 1.] So, we need to write [MATH: 0.3] in scientific notation, as follows:

[MATH: 0.3 = 3 \times 10^{-1}]

Therefore,

[MATH: − 0.3 × 10^{− 9}|= − (3 × 10^{− 1}) × 10^{− 9}; = − 3 × (10^{− 1} × 10^{− 9}); = − 3 × 10^{− 1 − 9}; = − 3 × 10^{− 10}.]

So, our final answer is [MATH: -3 \times 10^{-10}.]

The above number is not in scientific notation because [MATH: 0.3 \lt 1.] So, we need to write [MATH: 0.3] in scientific notation, as follows:
